# LiveQuakes

> Free, real-time earthquake tracker. The map and event list are built live
> in the visitor's browser from the USGS Earthquake Hazards Program's public
> GeoJSON feeds, plus reports from a community network of citizen-run
> seismometers.

LiveQuakes (https://livequakes.com/) shows recent earthquakes worldwide on an
interactive, zoomable world map and a sortable list, filterable by minimum
magnitude, time range (past hour / day / 7 days / 30 days), and place name.
It also supports "near me" distance filtering and browser notifications for
new quakes above a chosen magnitude.

All earthquake data comes directly from the USGS Earthquake Hazards Program
(https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/v1.0/) -- LiveQuakes does not
independently detect or verify earthquakes; it is a live viewer for USGS's
public data.

## Regional pages

Live earthquake pages filtered to individual U.S. states, each with a short
summary of the region's main earthquake sources and notable historic quakes:

- California: https://livequakes.com/california
- Nevada: https://livequakes.com/nevada
- Oregon: https://livequakes.com/oregon
- Washington: https://livequakes.com/washington
- Alaska: https://livequakes.com/alaska
- Hawaii: https://livequakes.com/hawaii

Individual earthquakes can be linked directly as
https://livequakes.com/#quake=<USGS event id>.

## Earthquake risk lookup

Visitors can enter a U.S. ZIP code (or use their location) to see the
long-term chance of strong, very strong, and severe shaking (Modified Mercalli
intensity VI, VII, VIII and above) over the next 50 years, from the USGS
National Seismic Hazard Model (2023 for the lower 48 and Alaska, 2021 for
Hawaii), for a typical stiff-soil site. Results also list M5+ earthquakes
within 50 km since 1950 and the distance to the nearest major plate boundary.
These are long-term forecasts, not predictions; LiveQuakes does not claim to
predict earthquakes. Shareable as https://livequakes.com/?zip=<ZIP>#risk.

## Community seismometer network

Anyone who owns a seismometer (Raspberry Shake, DIY accelerometer-based
sensor, etc.) can register it on LiveQuakes and have it report ground-motion
events, shown on the same map as community station markers alongside the
official USGS data. Registration and event ingestion happen via a simple
HTTPS API (station registration returns a per-station API key; events are
POSTed as JSON with an amplitude and duration).

## Key facts

- Data source: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program (public domain feeds)
- Coverage: global
- Update frequency: user-configurable auto-refresh (30s / 1min / 5min) plus manual refresh
- Cost: free, no account required to view; a free account (Google sign-in) is only needed to register a community seismometer station
- Privacy: earthquake data is fetched client-side in the visitor's own browser; nothing about page views is sent to or stored by LiveQuakes
